subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add true soft-steer semantics beyond current boundary steering, and should that be a new queue mode, an opt-in policy, or explicitly out of scope for now?
rationale: The requested behavior would change when active runs may be interrupted, how partial output and tool results are preserved, and which session context receives injected input; current docs intentionally define boundary steering and separate interrupt behavior.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Define a new mode or policy for abort/capture/inject/resume semantics, with explicit tests for streaming, tools, fallback, transcript state, and channel-visible behavior.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering Only
options.body: Close or narrow the feature direction and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003 for remaining boundary-steering ingress bugs.

options.title: Change Steer Globally
options.body: Make existing steer more aggressive by default, accepting compatibility risk for users who expect current tool-boundary behavior.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Define a new mode or policy for abort/capture/inject/resume semantics, with explicit tests for streaming, tools, fallback, transcript state, and channel-visible behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already handled the recent product/runtime review on this issue, and the unresolved decision is queue-mode lifecycle direction rather than a single owner-file fix.
